title: Impersonal 6: Reflexive Impersonals (хочется, кажется, удаётся)
titleRussian: Безличные 6: Безличные возвратные глаголы (хочется, кажется, удаётся)
description: A small family of verbs ending in -ся build impersonal sentences with no nominative subject. Хочется reports a soft feeling of wanting (compare the deliberate хочу). Кажется reports a tentative opinion. Удаётся reports a success. The structure: dative person (optional) + the reflexive verb in the 3rd-singular neuter form, often with a complement.
descriptionRussian: Небольшая семья возвратных глаголов на -ся образует безличные предложения без подлежащего в именительном падеже. «Хочется» сообщает о мягком желании (сравните намеренное «хочу»). «Кажется» сообщает осторожное мнение. «Удаётся» сообщает об успехе. Структура: дательный падеж лица (по желанию) + возвратный глагол в форме 3-го лица единственного числа среднего рода, обычно с дополнением.
intro: These use a reflexive verb frozen in one form, and the most useful of them draws a distinction English cannot. There is a verb for wanting something deliberately and another for merely feeling like it, and the two never mix. There is also a complaint frame that exists almost only in the negative: not sleeping, not working, nothing going right.
rules: Structure: (dative person) + reflexive verb in the 3rd-singular form + complement (genitive, infinitive, or что clause). The verb stays neuter singular whatever the person's gender.
Хочется carries a soft 'feels like' reading; хочу carries a deliberate 'wants' reading. They never mix: «Я хочется» is wrong, «Мне хочу» is wrong.
Кажется attributes a tentative opinion. It pairs with a что clause or a short stand-alone form ('Кажется, идёт дождь').
Удаётся takes a dative person plus an infinitive and reports a success. The past form удалось is neuter singular regardless of the person's gender.
The complaint frame (не спится, не работается) is almost always negative and takes only a dative person, with no other complement.
examples: Мне хочется кофе. (I feel like some coffee.) Genitive object after хочется.
Антону хочется спать. (Anton feels like sleeping.) Infinitive complement after хочется.
Мне кажется, что Антон прав. (It seems to me that Anton is right.) Что clause after кажется.
Маше удаётся всё успевать. (Masha manages to get everything done.) Infinitive complement after удаётся.
Мне не спится. (I cannot fall asleep.) Complaint frame; no complement.
Мне не удалось купить билет. (I did not manage to buy a ticket.) Past form удалось is neuter singular regardless of the person's gender.

tables.title: The four reflexive impersonals at a glance

items.hint: Softer 'feels like'; impersonal frame with the dative person мне.
items.explanation: Хочется is the impersonal reflexive verb that pairs with a dative person (мне) and reports a soft feeling of wanting. Хочу would require я in the nominative ('Я хочу кофе') as a personal sentence.

items.promptEnglish: Masha manages to get everything done at work.
items.hint: Reports a success; impersonal frame with a dative person and an infinitive.
items.explanation: Удаётся reports a success in an impersonal construction (dative person Маше + infinitive успевать). Может would require Маша in the nominative ('Маша может'), a personal sentence. Хочется is the wanting reading. Трудно is the difficulty reading, the opposite of success.

items.promptEnglish: Today I cannot fall asleep at all.
items.hint: Complaint frame: a process is not happening for the person. Which is the 3rd-sg reflexive form?
items.explanation: Спится is the 3rd-singular reflexive form in the complaint frame, pairing with the dative person мне and almost always negative. Сплю would require я in the nominative ('я не сплю').

items.promptEnglish: It seems to me that Anton is right.
items.hint: Tentative opinion in an impersonal frame with a что clause.
items.explanation: Кажется attributes a tentative opinion in an impersonal construction; the dative мне names the person and the что clause carries the content. Думаю and знаю would build personal sentences with я in the nominative ('Я думаю, что'). Видит would need a nominative subject too and reads as 'X sees,' the wrong meaning.

items.promptEnglish: I cannot get any work done today.
items.hint: Complaint frame: a process is not happening for the person. Which is the 3rd-sg reflexive form?
items.explanation: Работается is the 3rd-singular reflexive form in the complaint frame, pairing with a dative person. The negative reading reports an internal block. Работаю would require я in the nominative.

items.prompt: Мне не _____ купить билет на концерт.
items.promptEnglish: I did not manage to buy a ticket to the concert.
items.hint: Past form of удаваться in an impersonal construction.
items.explanation: The past form of the impersonal reflexive удаваться / удаться is удалось, always neuter singular regardless of the dative person's gender. Удался and удалась are past forms that would agree with a nominative subject ('билет удался' = 'the ticket was a success'), a different sentence.

items.promptEnglish: I feel like sleeping although it is still early.
items.hint: A soft passing wish: dative + which verb + which form after it?
items.explanation: The soft wish is хочется + infinitive with a dative person: мне хочется спать. Хочу would need the nominative я; a finite verb cannot follow хочется.

items.promptEnglish: It seems to me that Anton is right.
items.hint: The tentative-opinion frame: which frozen verb + connector?
items.explanation: The frame is мне кажется, что...: the impersonal reflexive stays in the frozen 3sg form and a что clause follows. Кажусь means 'I seem (to someone)', a personal form the frame rejects.

items.promptEnglish: Masha managed to find a new job in a week.
items.hint: Past success: the frozen neuter form + what after it?
items.explanation: The past of удаться is always frozen neuter удалось plus a perfective infinitive: Маше удалось найти работу. Удалась wrongly agrees with Маша; a finite verb cannot follow удалось.

items.hint: The complaint frame: dative person + negative + which form?
items.explanation: The sleep-complaint frame is dative + не спится: Антону не спится ('sleep will not come to him'). Спит would need Антон as a nominative subject; the impersonal reflexive carries the 'can't manage it' shade.

blanks: Маше _____ спать, она устала. (Masha feels like sleeping, she is tired.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The English 'feels like' is the soft-wanting reading, which хочется carries in an impersonal construction with the dative person Маше. Хочет would need Маша in the nominative ('Маша хочет спать'), a personal sentence. Может is 'can,' the wrong modality. Трудно is the difficulty reading.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I sleep badly in the heat.
errorCorrection.explanation: With the dative person мне, the verb is the impersonal reflexive спится: мне плохо спится ('sleep does not come well to me'). The personal спит would need a nominative subject; сплю ('I sleep') would need я, not мне.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маше обычно удаёт находить время для спорта.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha usually manages to find time for sport.
errorCorrection.explanation: The impersonal verb удаваться keeps its reflexive -ся in every form: Маше удаётся. 'Удаёт' without -ся is not a Russian word.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My work goes well in the mornings.
errorCorrection.explanation: With the dative person мне, the verb is the impersonal reflexive работается: мне хорошо работается ('work goes well for me'). Работает is a personal form needing a nominative subject, and работаю would need я, not мне.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I feel like some coffee, I am very tired.
minimalPairs.explanation: Хочется is impersonal and takes a dative person (мне), not a nominative subject. The nominative я would require the personal verb хочу ('Я хочу кофе').

minimalPairs.context: Маше не _____ купить билет на концерт.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha did not manage to buy a ticket to the concert.
minimalPairs.explanation: Impersonal reflexive past forms are always neuter singular: удалось. The feminine form удалась would require a feminine nominative subject; it does not agree with the dative person.

sentenceBuilding.hint: Dative person + хочется + the genitive of the thing wanted.
sentenceBuilding.grammarFocus: Хочется takes the dative person (мне) plus the genitive of the thing wanted (чая). The personal я хочу would instead take the accusative чай.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Anton managed to pass the exam.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Dative person + neuter-singular past удалось + perfective infinitive.
sentenceBuilding.grammarFocus: Удалось is the neuter-singular past form regardless of the person's gender (Антон is masculine, but the verb does not change). It is followed by a perfective infinitive (сдать).

sentenceBuilding.translation: Lena can't get any work done today.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Complaint frame: dative person + не + the 3rd-singular reflexive verb, no other complement.
sentenceBuilding.grammarFocus: The complaint frame is dative person (Лене) + не + the 3rd-singular reflexive verb (работается), almost always negative and with no other complement.

reviewVocab.definition: feels like (impersonal reflexive verb; dative person + genitive object or infinitive; softer than the personal хочу)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Мне хочется кофе' слово 'хочется' выражает мягкое желание, а не намерение.

reviewVocab.definition: seems / it seems (impersonal reflexive verb; dative person + что clause; tentative or hedged opinion)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Мне кажется, что Антон прав' слово 'кажется' выражает мнение говорящего.

reviewVocab.definition: manages / succeeded (impersonal reflexive verb; dative person + infinitive; past form удалось is always neuter singular)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маше удалось закончить работу вовремя' форма 'удалось' стоит в среднем роде единственного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: cannot fall asleep / cannot get work done (complaint-frame impersonal reflexives; dative person only, almost always negative, no other complement)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Мне не спится' глагол стоит в безличной форме и сообщает, что человек не может заснуть.
